title: Cyclone Akvan at peak strength, IMD says; landfall between Narsapur and Puri on Friday
dek: The IMD's 5.30 am bulletin says the storm has slowed to 5 kmph and will not strengthen further before it crosses north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha around Friday noon at 90-100 kmph; south Bengal faces heavy rain on Friday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclone Akvan has reached its peak strength and will not intensify further, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said early on Thursday, as the storm crawled north over the Bay of Bengal towards a landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on Friday, 20 November. The IMD's National Bulletin No. 28, issued at 5.30 am, keeps a cyclone warning with a "red message" for the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts and forecasts that Akvan will cross as a severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, weakening to 70-80 kmph by late Friday morning.

The storm slowed to 5 kmph overnight, from about 9 kmph on Wednesday afternoon, and at 2.30 am lay about 470 km east-south-east of Narsapur, 490 km south-south-east of Kalingapatnam, 580 km south of Gopalpur and 640 km south of Puri. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the system had attained its peak intensity, according to reports. Overnight the IMD dropped the strengthening it had forecast on Wednesday evening, when its table showed winds of up to 100-110 kmph on Thursday. Gangetic West Bengal still faces heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on Friday, and Odisha has put five districts on red alert from Thursday, according to reports.

## Latest bulletin

The IMD's forecast table in its 5.30 am bulletin keeps the storm at 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph through Thursday as it moves north-north-west, easing to 85-95 kmph by 11.30 pm on Thursday and to a cyclonic storm of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph by 11.30 am on Friday. It expects Akvan to weaken to a depression by Friday night, near 21.6°N over Odisha, a track that runs north towards Odisha and Jharkhand rather than inland over Telangana and Chhattisgarh.

On Wednesday evening the IMD had shifted the expected crossing north from the stretch between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, which it had forecast since Tuesday evening, to the Narsapur-Puri window, which runs from south of Kakinada past Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur to Puri. Gale winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph are expected along and off the north Odisha and West Bengal coasts from Thursday forenoon until Friday noon, the IMD said.

A storm surge of 0.5 to 1 metre above the astronomical tide is very likely to flood low-lying areas of West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam districts in Andhra Pradesh and Ganjam and Puri districts in Odisha at landfall, the IMD said. Along the north Odisha and West Bengal coasts, gale winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph are expected from Thursday morning until Friday noon.

The IMD's Wednesday evening bulletin warned of "major damage" to thatched and kutcha houses, power and communication poles, and standing crops and plantations in north coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha, waves of 9-14 metres from Thursday becoming "phenomenal" above 14 metres from Thursday night until landfall, flooding of escape routes and disruption to rail, road and air traffic. It advised a total suspension of fishing and offshore operations and that people living in coastal huts be moved to safer places.

Odisha placed Puri, Ganjam, Kendrapara, Kandhamal and Gajapati districts on red alert from Thursday and nine more districts on orange alert on Wednesday, and sent four senior IAS officers to oversee preparations in Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Kendrapara and Gajapati, according to reports. The state has identified 2,04,070 people, 1,21,597 of them in Ganjam district, for possible evacuation, has deployed 74 rescue teams from its own disaster response force and the NDRF, and has been releasing water from dams for two days, reports said. Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the storm could cross anywhere between Kalingapatnam, Gopalpur and Puri, according to reports.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings in the IMD's 5.30 am bulletin on Thursday, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) on 19 and 20 November; heavy rain at isolated places in north coastal Andhra Pradesh on 21 November.
- Odisha: heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls over south Odisha, and heavy to very heavy rain over north Odisha, on 19 and 20 November; heavy rain at isolated places on 21 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: heavy rain at isolated places on 19 and 21 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 20 November. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata expects 7-20 cm at one or two places in East and West Midnapore on Friday.
- Eastern Telangana: heavy rain at isolated places on 20 November.
- Jharkhand: heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November; Chhattisgarh on 20 and 21 November; east Vidarbha and east Madhya Pradesh on 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and preparations

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest Bay of Bengal until 20 November, the westcentral Bay until the morning of 21 November, the eastcentral Bay until 19 November, and the northwest Bay, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, until the morning of 21 November, the IMD said, and to suspend fishing operations totally in those areas.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials on Monday to deploy National and State Disaster Response Force teams in advance, keep power staff ready and divert floodwater into reservoirs, according to reports. Odisha has alerted all 30 of its districts and opened round-the-clock control rooms, reports said.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. Akvan's name was proposed by Iran, according to the published list of north Indian Ocean cyclone names.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast. The IMD's earliest outlooks pointed further north, towards the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; its bulletins from Monday moved the expected crossing south, to between Nellore and Visakhapatnam by Tuesday evening, before the IMD moved it back north on Wednesday afternoon, to between Narsapur and Puri, and lowered the expected strength at landfall twice.

## What happens next

The IMD has moved from a cyclone alert to a cyclone warning with a red message for the stretch of coast where landfall is expected; its next step is a post-landfall outlook. It issues national bulletins every three hours. The landfall point may still shift within the Narsapur-Puri window.

## Key numbers

- 490 km: distance from Kalingapatnam at 2.30 am IST on Thursday
- 640 km: distance from Puri
- 5 kmph: the storm's speed overnight
- Around noon, 20 November: forecast landfall between Narsapur and Puri
- 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 0.5-1 metre: forecast storm surge in six Andhra Pradesh and two Odisha districts
- 5: Odisha districts on red alert from 19 November
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha on 19-20 November
